seo.title: React Launch Checklist: 32 Essential Steps
seo.description: Ship your React app confidently with this 32-step launch checklist. Covers build config, testing, accessibility, performance, security, and deployment.

introduction: Launching a React application involves more than passing your test suite. From build optimization and error boundaries to accessibility compliance and security hardening, there are dozens of details that can make or break your launch. This 30-step checklist ensures your React app is production-grade across every dimension.

sections.name: Build & Configuration
sections.description: Verify your React project is properly configured for a production build with no warnings or misconfigurations.

items.text: Run production build with zero errors and warnings
items.description: Execute your build command and resolve every warning. Build warnings often indicate actual bugs — unused imports, missing keys, deprecated APIs — that manifest as runtime issues in production.

items.text: Enable React Strict Mode
items.description: Wrap your root component with `<React.StrictMode>`. It double-invokes effects and renders in development to catch impure components, missing cleanup functions, and deprecated API usage before they cause production bugs.

items.text: Verify production environment variables
items.description: Ensure all API URLs, feature flags, and configuration values are set for production. Check that development-only variables (debug flags, test API keys) are not leaking into the production bundle.

items.text: Remove all console.log statements and debug code
items.description: Search for console.log, console.warn, debugger statements, and TODO comments. Use an ESLint rule like `no-console` set to error for production builds. Debug output in production leaks implementation details.

items.text: Configure source maps for production debugging
items.description: Generate source maps during build but do not serve them publicly. Upload them to your error tracking service (Sentry, Bugsnag) so stack traces are readable. Use hidden-source-map mode in your bundler.

items.text: Set up path aliases for clean imports
items.description: Configure `@/` or `~/` path aliases in your tsconfig.json and bundler config. This eliminates fragile relative imports like `../../../components/Button` and makes refactoring easier post-launch.

sections.name: Error Handling & Resilience
sections.description: Make your app resilient to runtime errors, network failures, and edge cases that only appear in production.

items.text: Add Error Boundaries around critical UI sections
items.description: Wrap major sections (sidebar, main content, widgets) with Error Boundaries so a crash in one section does not take down the entire page. Show a meaningful fallback UI with a retry button, not a white screen.

items.text: Handle loading and error states for all data fetches
items.description: Every component that fetches data should handle loading (skeleton or spinner), error (retry button with error message), and empty (helpful empty state) scenarios. Use React Query or SWR for built-in state management.

items.text: Implement global error tracking
items.description: Set up Sentry, Bugsnag, or similar to capture unhandled errors and promise rejections. Configure user context, breadcrumbs, and source maps. Set up alerts for new error types and error rate spikes.

items.text: Add offline detection and graceful degradation
items.description: Listen for `online`/`offline` events and show a banner when the user loses connection. Queue failed requests for retry when connectivity returns. Use the `navigator.onLine` API for initial state.

items.text: Test edge cases: empty data, long strings, special characters
items.description: Test with empty arrays, null values, extremely long text, Unicode characters, and RTL text. These edge cases cause layout breaks, truncation bugs, and crashes that only appear with real user data.

sections.name: Testing & Quality
sections.description: Verify your application works correctly across different scenarios, browsers, and devices before going live.

items.text: Achieve meaningful test coverage for critical paths
items.description: Write integration tests for your core user flows — signup, login, checkout, main feature usage. Use React Testing Library for component tests that verify behavior, not implementation. Aim for 80% coverage on critical paths.

items.text: Run end-to-end tests with Playwright or Cypress
items.description: Write E2E tests for your 5-10 most important user journeys. Run them against your staging environment before every release. E2E tests catch integration issues that unit tests miss — broken API contracts, auth flows, navigation.

items.text: Test across major browsers and devices
items.description: Test on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge at minimum. Test on iOS Safari and Android Chrome for mobile. Use BrowserStack or LambdaTest for devices you do not have. Safari WebKit differences cause the most cross-browser bugs.

items.text: Verify all forms validate correctly
items.description: Test every form with empty submissions, invalid email formats, too-short passwords, special characters, and SQL injection attempts. Verify that validation messages are clear and that the form prevents submission until all errors are fixed.

items.text: Run ESLint and TypeScript checks with zero errors
items.description: Configure ESLint with `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` and `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`. Run `tsc --noEmit` to verify type safety. Both should be part of your CI pipeline and block deployments on failure.

sections.name: Performance Optimization
sections.description: Optimize your React app's load time and runtime performance before real users hit it.

items.text: Code-split routes with React.lazy and Suspense
items.description: Wrap route components with `React.lazy(() => import('./Page'))` and a `<Suspense>` boundary. This splits your bundle per route so users only download the code for the page they are visiting.

items.text: Optimize images with responsive srcsets
items.description: Serve images at appropriate sizes for each viewport. Use `<picture>` with WebP/AVIF sources and fallback. Add `loading='lazy'` to below-the-fold images and `fetchpriority='high'` to hero images.

items.text: Audit and reduce bundle size
items.description: Use `source-map-explorer` or `webpack-bundle-analyzer` to visualize your bundle. Target under 200KB gzipped for initial load. Look for large dependencies, duplicated packages, and unused exports.

items.text: Profile with React DevTools and fix performance issues
items.description: Use the React DevTools Profiler to record user interactions and identify components that re-render unnecessarily. Fix with React.memo, useMemo, or by restructuring state to minimize re-render scope.

items.text: Preload critical assets
items.description: Add `<link rel='preload'>` for fonts, critical CSS, and above-the-fold images. Use `<link rel='prefetch'>` for likely next-page resources. This tells the browser to start fetching before the rendering code requests them.

sections.name: Security & Deployment
sections.description: Harden your application against common vulnerabilities and set up a reliable deployment pipeline.

items.text: Sanitize all user-generated content
items.description: Never use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with unsanitized input. If you must render HTML, sanitize it with DOMPurify first. This prevents XSS attacks where attackers inject malicious scripts through form inputs or URL parameters.

items.text: Secure API communication with HTTPS and CORS
items.description: Ensure all API requests use HTTPS. Configure your API's CORS policy to only allow requests from your production domain. Never use `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` in production.

items.text: Implement proper authentication token storage
items.description: Store JWTs in httpOnly cookies, not localStorage. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript on the page, including XSS payloads. HttpOnly cookies are invisible to client-side JavaScript.

items.text: Set up CI/CD pipeline with automated checks
items.description: Configure GitHub Actions to run lint, type-check, tests, and build on every PR. Add Lighthouse CI for performance regression detection. Block merges when any check fails.

items.text: Configure CDN caching with proper cache headers
items.description: Set long cache TTLs (1 year) for hashed static assets (JS, CSS, images). Set short TTLs or no-cache for HTML files. This ensures users get updated HTML that references the latest asset hashes.

items.text: Run npm audit and fix vulnerabilities
items.description: Execute `npm audit` and address all high and critical severity vulnerabilities. Use `npm audit fix` for compatible updates. For breaking changes, evaluate each package and update manually or find alternatives.

sections.name: Final Pre-Launch Verification
sections.description: Last round of checks to catch anything missed in earlier stages.

items.text: Test all user flows end-to-end on staging
items.description: Walk through every major user journey on your staging environment: registration, login, core features, payment, logout. Test on both mobile and desktop. Have someone outside the development team do this too.

items.text: Verify analytics and tracking are firing correctly
items.description: Open your analytics tool's real-time view and navigate through your staging site. Verify page views, events, and conversions are tracked. Missing analytics on launch day means losing data you can never recover.

items.text: Set up uptime and performance monitoring
items.description: Configure uptime monitoring (Better Stack, UptimeRobot) and real-user monitoring (Sentry Performance, Datadog RUM). Set alert thresholds for response time degradation and error rate spikes.

items.text: Verify SEO essentials: meta tags, OG images, and canonical URLs
items.description: Check every page for unique title tags, meta descriptions under 160 characters, Open Graph images for social sharing, and canonical URLs. Missing meta tags on launch day means search engines index incomplete information that is hard to correct later.

items.text: Prepare a rollback plan and document the deployment process
items.description: Write down the exact steps to revert to the previous version if something goes wrong. Include database migration rollbacks, feature flag toggles, and DNS changes. Under launch-day pressure, a documented rollback plan prevents panicked improvisation.

tips: Create a staging environment that mirrors production exactly — same hosting, same environment variables, same third-party integrations. Test every deployment on staging before promoting to production.
Use feature flags (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, or a simple JSON config) to decouple deployment from release. Deploy code to production with features disabled, then enable them gradually.
Schedule your launch for a Tuesday or Wednesday morning, never Friday afternoon. You want maximum team availability if issues arise, and weekday traffic patterns help you spot anomalies quickly.
Keep a launch day runbook with step-by-step deployment instructions, rollback procedures, and emergency contacts. Under pressure, you will forget obvious steps.
Set up a dedicated Slack channel or war room for launch day. Centralize all communication — scattered discussions across DMs and threads cause confusion and slow response times.
